terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.solveMethod: Solved by silhouette overlay across an azimuth x elevation sweep, scored on two scale-free ratios (facadeRun:sideRun and height:facadeRun) plus subject-bbox aspect. At azimuth 34 / elevation 22 the model measures facade:side 2.046 against the plate's 1.960, height:facade 1.088 against 1.111, and a subject-aspect delta of 0.000.
referenceCamera.correction: An earlier solve put elevation at 13 on the visual impression that the plate was shot low. That was wrong - the plate shows a substantial band of roof deck - and at elevation 13 the model measured height:facade 1.002 against 1.111, which read as the model being ~14% too short. That apparent shortfall was the WRONG CAMERA, not a proportion error: at the correct elevation the residual is about 2%.
referenceCamera.harnessLimitation: The thaikit harness frames at 0.92 of the tangent fit (render/harness.html), which clips props wider than they are tall. This building touches x=0 at azimuths 34-38. The clipping is a few pixels here, but it is worth knowing for a kit with many wide buildings and road tiles.

objectClass.notes: Facade faces +Z; the wall carrying the personnel door, bulkhead lamp and casement window is +X. Asymmetric: the glazed bay rhythm is not mirrored about the centre line and the +X openings have no -X counterpart. The ONLY saturated region on the whole building is the fascia graphic, which is what makes it identity-defining.

details.description: Horizontal stripe band, orange over white over green, forming an end block each side of a white centre field, running the full lightbox width.
Red numeral 7 with green ELEVEN overprinted across its lower half, small registered-trademark glyph at lower right, centred in the white field.
Raised white perimeter frame around the lightbox face, standing proud of the graphic plane.
Two brackets on the lightbox return holding it clear of the spandrel; the shadow gap behind the tray is visible.
Chamfered white cap projecting proud of both parapet faces with a drip edge.
Grey membrane deck sitting below the coping line, inside the parapet upstand.
Dark horizontal louvre panel on the condenser's +X face. CONCAVE feature: per the microscope rule it must not be colour-gated, since a dark ratio there reads cavity shading, not material.
Raised circular cowl ring on the condenser top face.
Short block feet lifting the casing clear of the deck, leaving a visible shadow gap.
Rectangular galvanised duct with raised transverse flange ribs at intervals.
Vertical aluminium mullions dividing the glazed wall into five bays; spacing is NOT uniform and the sliding pair sits left of centre.
Recessed white header box above the sliding pair, carrying the track.
Horizontal pull handle on the leading sliding leaf.
Row of small saturated red/yellow/green tabs applied to the glass at approx 1.2 m above the sill, continuing across every bay.
Personnel door set in a surround standing slightly proud of the render.
Lever handle on the door's leading edge at approx 1.05 m.
Small rectangular wall-mounted light box projecting from the +X wall above the door head.
Two-pane casement on +X, taller than wide, with a central vertical mullion and a proud frame.
Darker grey band approx 0.15 m tall wrapping the wall base with a hard top edge.
White piers flanking the glazed opening, framing the shopfront within the facade.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness

qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.

referencePbrExtraction.reason:
Extraction WAS performed for all thirteen materials and every one cleared 0.7 (see each material's referencePbr block and material-evidence/). What is deliberately NOT done is BINDING those outputs as a runtime texture set.
The crops are scene photographs, not tileable material samples: render-white_albedo.png is a crop of the +X elevation containing the personnel door, the casement window and the plinth. Bound as a tiling map it would smear a picture of a door across every wall of the building, and it carries the plate's baked key light and occlusion into base colour, which the material brief forbids outright.
The skill's own rule decides this: solid albedo for flat paint, a projected de-lit reference crop for anything patterned or printed. This building is flat paint, bare glass and mill-finish metal everywhere EXCEPT the brand fascia - and the fascia does go through the projection route, as a generated canvas texture drawn from measured albedo and measured layout (projection-route.json).
Evidence is preserved per material under referencePbr.evidenceMaps rather than referencePbr.maps: the generator treats a complete five-map set as an instruction to bind textures, and that is a different claim from 'PBR evidence was extracted'.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

lookDevTargets.toneMappingRationale: ACES keeps the illuminated fascia's white face from clipping to flat paper against a building that is otherwise near-white. Linear exposure blew the bezel and the face to the same value, which erases the one cue that the box is lit.

contactShadow.notes: Floor-placed prop, so it needs a ground contact shadow or it reads as hovering. Separately, the condenser feet and the fascia stand-off each cast a small local shadow - those gaps are identity features and disappear without shadowing.

lookDevTargets.environmentRationale: The harness supplies directional lights and no environment map, so metals cannot produce a broad reflected highlight. Aluminium and galvanised roughness are authored for that, and any specular shortfall against the plate must NOT be compensated by lifting albedo.

actionReadiness.rationale: Three pivots and one socket, each named for a mechanism. The building is a static shell whose ONLY moving parts are the two sliding entrance leaves; every other component declares animationRole 'static' and no pivot. The single socket is where the brand fascia attaches, which fourteen buildings sharing this module already depend on. No pivot is named for a place on the surface.

assumptions: Declared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m is the registry contract and overrides the Meshy proxy. The proxy's ratios (1.000:0.783:1.069 vs declared 1.000:0.575:0.875) disagree because its height includes the rooftop plant and its depth is inflated by single-view hallucination - it cannot see the back and guesses.
4.6 m is TOTAL height including rooftop plant: coping top 4.00 m, condenser top 4.45 m, fan cowl 4.55 m. This reconciliation is what makes the declared height internally consistent with the plate.

-X side wall is unseen (confidence 0.30): built plain render + plinth. The +X door, lamp and window are deliberately NOT mirrored - the subject is asymmetric and a mirrored opening would be invented detail.
-Z rear wall is unseen (confidence 0.30): built plain render + plinth, speculative.
Roof deck aft of the condenser is occluded (confidence 0.45): plain membrane, no invented plant.

Interior fitout is built shallow and legible rather than dimensionally accurate (confidence 0.50). It exists because a dark void behind the glazing reads as a false front, which is its own fidelity failure.
Parapet coping is built as a chamfered cap with a drip edge (confidence 0.60), read from the roof-plant evidence region.
Suitability is recorded CONDITIONAL rather than pass: the plate is an excellent three-quarter view, but half the envelope is unseen and the trademark glyphs are approximated.

Every item formerly listed under unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation was decided, not dropped; the decisions are these assumptions and the risks below, and the original list is preserved in resolved-unknowns.json.

Components are parented to the root rather than to building-shell. The shell carries a -90 degree X rotation so its plan profile extrudes upward, and transform inheritance would rotate every child with it. attachment.parentId keeps the logical hierarchy intact.

Parapet coping sits at 4.25 m (raised from 4.00 m), with the condenser topping out at 4.60 m so the declared total height is spent on the wall rather than left to the rooftop unit. The change was originally motivated by a measurement taken at the wrong camera elevation, which overstated the shortfall as ~17%; at the solved camera the residual is about 2%. The raise is kept because it is still in the right direction and stays inside the declared 4.6 m envelope, but the evidence for it is much weaker than first recorded.

Facade layout is MEASURED, not assumed: the glazed run spans 12.5%-87.3% of the facade width (1.0 m pier each side, 6.0 m opening) with the head at 0.739 of wall height (3.14 m) and the sill at the plinth. It is FOUR bays of 1.5 m with a centred sliding pair - an earlier draft read five bays with the pair left of centre, from the wide shot rather than from a scan.

The component tree is FLAT at the transform level: every component parents to the root and records its logical parent in attachment.parentId instead. Positions here are world metres, so nesting added the parent's offset on top - it put the rooftop plant at y 7.78 and the fascia graphic at z 7.28.

Buildings in this kit are EXTERIOR SHELLS by direction: no interior geometry. The lit interior volume and the ten instanced shelf decks are removed. The glazing is therefore treated as a surface in its own right - a tinted, mostly opaque pane - rather than as a window onto a modelled shop, which is both cheaper and the only way glass can read correctly with nothing behind it.

componentTree.name: Building shell: three solid walls
componentTree.topologyRationale: The three solid walls are one continuous painted render surface and one extrusion. Splitting them into three components would cost three draw calls, for the life of the prop, to express one skin. The +Z wall is separate ONLY because a plan extrude cannot carry a vertical opening, and the shopfront opening is an identity feature.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: U-shaped footprint ring extruded 4.0 m upward: the -X, -Z and +X walls at 0.20 m thickness, open on +Z where the shopfront wall takes over. Hollow by construction, which is what lets the interior read through the glazing.

copingProfile.note: Chamfered cap with a drip edge, measured from zone-r0c1 at 0.75 confidence.

geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: Eight profile points, one extrusion step, no bevel: 8 side quads plus caps, roughly 60 triangles.
geometryDescriptor.shapeSpaceNote: Profile is authored in (sx, sy) = (worldX, -worldZ). The component carries rotationEuler [-pi/2, 0, 0], which maps the shape plane onto the ground plane and the extrusion axis onto world +Y. Extrude components are NOT unit-scaled by the generator - profile units are real metres - so the numbers here are the building's actual footprint.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Depth separation against z-fighting: two surfaces facing the SAME direction in the SAME plane flicker as the camera moves, and every one of these was authored flush at exactly z=3.500. The U's open ends sat at z=3.5, coplanar and co-facing with the facade wall's front face, so the two front corners flickered. They now stop at z=3.3, the facade wall's back face, which is a butt joint of opposed faces - and the footprint comes out at exactly the declared 7.0 m.

textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely. That function builds FIVE canvases per material at textureResolution, pixel by pixel in JavaScript with multi-octave noise: at 1024 it produced 34 textures totalling 35.1 megapixels and took 24 SECONDS inside createObjectModel before the preview could appear, scaling as the square of the resolution (256 -> 1.6 s, 512 -> 6.5 s, 1024 -> 26 s). It also cost ~64 MB of VRAM on a kit aimed at low-end integrated GPUs. And it was not merely wasteful: the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 whenever a texture set exists, discarding the authored albedo and the reference-derived roughness - which is what rendered this white building mid-grey and forced the palette re-centring recorded above.

reviewHistory.summary: Z-fighting sweep. The reported flicker on the door border was the shopfront frame's front face and the facade wall's front face both at exactly z=3.500, co-facing, overlapping 6.20 x 3.19 m. A bounding-box scan found five more exact same-facing coplanar pairs (shell ends vs facade wall, door leaves vs glazing back over 3.00 x 2.53 m, fascia tray back vs wall, condenser vs duct bottoms, side door vs plinth top). Two further cases were INVISIBLE to that scan because they are interior profile edges rather than envelope faces, and had to be read off zoomed renders: the frame ring's bottom rail top face on the plinth top (torn sill), and the ring's hole edges exactly on the opening reveal at x=+/-3.0 and y=3.14 (stippled jambs). All now separated; the scan reports clean at 1 mm. Two defects fixed themselves in the process: the fascia's declared 0.06 m stand-off shadow gap now physically exists, and the frame's bottom rail became the real KICKPLATE, closing a 0.20 m slot under the glazing that looked straight into the empty shell.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero4x class and none was invented. Designed to in the BLOCKOUT: the component split was chosen against the draw-call ceiling before any geometry existed, which is why the feet, cowls, brackets and pull handle are folded into their parents rather than left as parts to merge later - a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: The facade wall had to split from the plan-extruded shell - a footprint profile cannot carry a vertical opening, and the shopfront opening is an identity feature worth one draw call. That was paid for by folding the condenser louvre face back into the casing as a material layer.

uniqueGeometries.note: CORRECTED. An earlier draft claimed 9 on the grounds that most components are scaled instances of one shared unit box. That was wrong: the generator applies real dimensions via geometry.scale(), which bakes into vertex data, so every scaled box is a genuinely distinct geometry. The honest count is one per component - 16 boxes and extrusions - and this axis is now the binding constraint on the prop, ahead of draw calls. The four repetition systems add none: each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: Triangles are NOT the binding constraint for this prop - unique geometries are, at 16 of 16. The large triangle headroom is deliberately available for silhouette work (coping chamfer, tray bevel, cowl segments) and must not be read as an invitation to split components, which would spend the axis that is actually scarce.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: Single soft key from front-upper-+X. Shadow under the coping and beneath the condenser feet gives its elevation.
Broad cool fill; keeps the -X-facing render off black.
Backdrop luma measures 0.58; ambient set so the render never falls under it, which the turntable gate would read as an interior hole.
The fascia is an internally illuminated box, which is why its face reads flatter than the render beside it. Emission, not a scene light.

ACES filmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0. Linear exposure clipped the lit fascia face and its bezel to the same white, erasing the one cue that the box is illuminated. Contact/ground shadow is on: this is a floor-placed prop that reads as hovering without it, and the condenser-foot and fascia stand-off gaps are identity features that vanish unshadowed.

A cool rim from behind-and--Z, which is what separates the parapet coping and the condenser from the backdrop. Without it the coping's top arris merges into the matte at the review azimuth and the roof reads as a flat plate rather than a walled deck.

Deliberately NONE. The thaikit harness supplies three directional lights and no environment map, and a host page may do the same, so nothing in this prop may depend on an environment to look right. That is why the metals are authored at metalness 0.15-0.35 rather than near 1: a near-1 metalness has no diffuse term and renders BLACK with nothing to reflect, which is how the shopfront framing was mistaken for tinted glazing for two passes.

proceduralStrategy: Axis-aligned primitives with boolean openings; one shared unit box scaled per component so most components cost a draw call but no additional unique geometry.
One generated canvas texture for the fascia graphic. No external image assets - the bundle imports a bare 'three' and nothing else.
Four repetition systems emitting InstancedMesh: shopfront mullions, sliding leaves, gondola shelf decks, manifestation tabs.
The whole building is orthogonal, so primitives and extrusions carry it with no implicit surfaces or sculpting; the only curved geometry on the prop is the two condenser fan cowls.
Product behind the glass is vertex-coloured banding on the instanced decks, never modelled items.

risks.note: Half the building's envelope is inferred. Reported as confidence 0.30, not claimed.
The 7 and ELEVEn glyphs are drawn from font/path, not traced from the trademark artwork. Colour, layout and proportion are measured; glyph outline is an approximation.
Every silhouette-based gate will pass trivially. Do not read a high silhouette score as fidelity for this subject.
The -X and -Z elevations and the aft roof deck are inference at 0.30-0.45 confidence. Reported, never claimed as observed.
The reference mesh disagrees with the declared scale on two axes. Declared wins; the proxy is logged as a disagreeing witness rather than obeyed.
analyze_texture.py flattened all thirteen materials to roughness base 0.9, which is its default and not a measurement. Observed values were restored by hand; the extracted roughness MAPS were kept.

The prop sits at exactly 16 of 16 unique geometries with no headroom. Any future component added to this building must replace one or go through a repetitionSystem; it cannot simply be appended. render-model.mjs measures the built scene and is the number that decides.

Extracted PBR maps are recorded as evidence but not bound as textures. Binding them was tried and produced a fully black building: the maps fail to resolve in the harness, and a failed texture samples black. Even resolved they were wrong - scene crops, not tileable samples.

A material with fewer than two resolvable palette colours silently renders through a hardcoded olive/tan procedural fallback rather than its own albedo. Every material here now declares colorVariation.palette from its measured crop. Worth checking on any future prop: the failure looks like a material choice, not a bug.

At the solved camera (azimuth 34 / elevation 22) the model's height:facade is 1.088 against the plate's 1.111 and the plan ratio agrees to ~4%, so the declared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m module and the plate agree closely. The Meshy proxy still disagrees (height ratio 0.783 vs 0.575), and it remains the outlier rather than the plate. Downgraded from medium after the camera solve was corrected.

render/harness.html frames at 0.92 of the tangent fit, so a prop wider than it is tall can touch the frame edge. This building clips by a few pixels at the review azimuth. Not corrected here because the harness is shared by every prop in the kit.

Metals authored near metalness 1 render black in the thaikit harness, which has no environment map. The shopfront framing did exactly that and was mistaken for tinted glazing. Aluminium, galvanised steel and the louvre face are authored at 0.35/0.30/0.15 so they read without IBL. Worth knowing for every metal prop in this kit.

analyze_texture.py's texturePalette is raw sampled pixels, not de-lit albedo, and the generator uses it to paint the procedural albedo map. Nine of thirteen materials here came back with palette means 50-100 luma from their measured base - render-white by 104 - so the prop rendered grey where the plate is white. Palettes are now re-centred on base albedo. This will affect every prop in the kit that uses analyze_texture.

Interiors are removed by direction. The plate shows shelving through the glass, so this is a deliberate divergence from the reference, not an omission: the glazing is authored as a tinted pane instead. Anything that later wants a visible interior must add it back as its own prop.

Components authored flush against one another put two same-facing surfaces in one plane, which tears and flickers as the camera moves. SIX pairs were built that way here. A bounding-box scan (scratch/<id>/coplanar.mjs) catches the envelope cases, but it is blind to interior profile edges - the worst one, the frame ring's bottom rail against the plinth top, had to be read off a zoomed render. Butt joints of OPPOSED faces are fine; it is co-facing coplanar surfaces that fight.
